Welcome back! OpenAI's agents cracked a Millennium Prize Problem, Anthropic's alignment lead put a percentage on human extinction, and Meta shipped an agent with a bodyguard.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: ChatGPT solved a $1 million math problem: Why is OpenAI refusing to take the prize money? Anthropic's science lead says we could all be dead in 10 years: What number did he put on it, and what did he say Anthropic doesn't have? Meta built a second agent to watch the first one: What does Sentinel stop Muse from doing? ChatGPT images got a whole lot better: Which upgrade finally fixes the thing every image model gets wrong? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. ChatGPT claims a Millennium Prize problem  One of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, open for roughly 90 years, each carrying a $1 million prize. Second one ever resolved. The equations describe how fluids move and they sit underneath weather forecasting, aircraft design and blood flow models.  The open question was whether a fluid that starts out smooth can break down and produce infinite speed in finite time. The answer is yes.  The proof builds a vortex that spirals inward and stretches like spaghetti, shrinking and accelerating while its energy stays finite. Roughly 10,000 agents worked in parallel for 88 hours. Lean formalization and verification took another 17 hours, done by GPT-6 Astra. On this problem alone the agents sent 2.7 million messages and produced about 130 billion output tokens. Across all the problems they tried, 4.9 million messages and 300 billion tokens. The model behind it is internal and has only been training since August 28. Training is still running. OpenAI says it is significantly more capable than Astra, which shipped six days ago and had people calling it AGI. The agents also disproved regularity for the unforced Euler equations along the way, which took about 100 agents and 50 hours. Then the credit fight started.  Tristan Buckmaster at NYU and Levent Alpöge at Anthropic published hours earlier, and Buckmaster says OpenAI heard about their method and used it.  OpenAI says it launched the effort on September 1 after hearing a rumor it later connected to them, saw none of their work before publication, and offered them a joint announcement on September 6 along

78821.subject: Networking Tips To Turn Connections Into Opportunities
78821.body:
Forbes Edge

Автор: Forbes


Автор: Forbes

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/networking-tips-turn-connections-opportunities-forbes-magazine-vxv1c?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BX6wdLDbJQESaG3IE0dx%2F6g%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3-7URBiXMaZso1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mtu6erq3~1j-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mtu6erq3-1j
  
Landing a new job in today’s slow labor market is already a challenge for many professionals. But for Gen Z in particular, making the connections needed to get a foot in the door is another major barrier, new data from LinkedIn shows.  According to a LinkedIn survey of more than 18,000 professionals, Gen Z understands how important relationships are in finding a job, but 53% aren’t sure how to get started with building a network, and 52% struggle with turning their contacts into real connections.  I spoke to Kory Kantenga, LinkedIn’s Head of Economics, Americas, about the key networking tips he advises that all professionals follow to build meaningful connections that will advance their career.  Engage and Comment on Social Media: To build your network beyond simply clicking the “connect” button, Kantenga advises professionals to comment and like any content that a desired connection posts. He also says you should join any online professional networks that interest you. Once you’re added to a particular group, it’s important to share your thoughts and engage within that community to make your presence known. Stop Trying to Network Only With Executives: When building your network, it’s easy to feel like the more senior your connections are the better. But when starting out, Kantenga emphasizes that it’s important to network across your peer group, not just above it. This means networking with recent alumni of your college or university and networking with peers who have recently landed a job. In many cases, Kantenga says that these connections might be the ones more willing to offer their time and expertise.  Show What You Have to Offer: From sharing insight on what you think about emerging technologies or trends to discussing any projects you’ve worked on, Kantenga says that “sharing your knowledge and expertise and connecting it back to what other people are doing [is] how you bring value very early on in your career.” Understand That Relationships Aren’t Built Overnight: While it’s easy to place expectations and timelines on networking—especially when you’re trying to land a job—Kantenga wants professionals to understand that true connections aren’t built instantaneously. “You have to invest, you have to nurture it, and you have to water it constantly. That’s what posting, engaging and relationship building is for,” he adds. Read here to learn

78819.subject: Solana’s Missing Piece
78819.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Hey all, Happy Wednesday! Crypto’s weekly gains held up despite Tuesday’s pullback as oil approached $100 and Strategy paused BTC purchases again. We also look at Solana’s Alpenglow upgrade, what is coming to mainnet and what it could mean for SOL.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

US markets traded lower as they returned from the long Labor Day weekend, while crypto posted relatively modest losses. Brent approached $100 amid Tuesday’s renewed fighting, with US forces[ reporting](https://apnews.com/article/iran-tanker-navy-warship-dfc9a1d9c9a5b8bc7b47fcc004025e65) the destruction of five Iranian tankers and Iran responding with missile launches toward US targets in Jordan.

BTC fell 0.7% to around $79,000 following Monday’s 1.7% decline, while the S&P 500 lost 0.6%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.8% and gold declined 2.1%. Meme (3.9%), Crypto Miners (2.8%) and Privacy (1.7%) led, while Modular (-4.1%), Crypto Equities (-2.5%) and Lending (-2.4%) lagged, with 15 of 25 indices finishing lower. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5161a4ca-da8a-41f3-bb52-08a3c83963bc/image.png?t=1788959879)
Caption: 

Despite Tuesday’s broad pullback, all 25 sector indices remain higher over the past seven days, including 13 with double-digit gains. As we noted over the past week, Privacy has gained nearly 30% alongside ZEC’s rally, while Crypto Miners are up 26% as AI demand continues to shape the sector’s performance. Those weekly gains suggest appetite for risk has extended well beyond BTC. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/81b4ecb7-bc29-452a-8761-141b6c26262e/image.png?t=1788959879)
Caption: 

Notably, Strategy opened the week by [disclosing](http://www.strategy.com/press/strategy-repurchases-176-million-of-strc-and-increases-digital-credit-securities-repurchase-program-to-2-billion_09-08-2026) no further BTC purchases, just one week after buying 4,603 BTC to end a 10-week pause. Instead, the company spent $176.3M repurchasing STRC and doubled its digital credit buyback authorization to $2B. With MSTR trading at 0.87x NAV, Strategy prioritized reducing preferred dividend obligations over adding more BTC. That marks a change from the previous week, when it raised $602.8M through stock sales, using $369.7M to buy BTC and $151.8M to repurchase STRC. 

Crypto enters this week’s inflation releases
